key_insight: BridgeSRDA combines low-resolution forecasts with sparse, noisy observations to generate probabilistic high-resolution flow reconstructions at lower cost than a high-resolution ensemble filter.
engineering_relevance: The framework could make ensemble flow-state estimation more affordable while providing retrospective reconstructions and short-range nowcasts.
method: Train a neural network to learn forecast-informed stochastic transport.
Sample high-resolution analysis ensembles conditioned on low-resolution forecasts and observations.
Use each current analysis to initialize the next low-resolution forecast.
evidence_signal: Across ten independently initialized 3D quasi-geostrophic trajectories in an unseen narrow-jet regime, BridgeSRDA reduced the mean absolute error ratio by approximately 32.5% versus deterministic 4D-SRDA at training observation spacing; 30-member analyses took approximately 17 s versus 31 s for the high-resolution filter.
watch_item: Uncertainty remains undercalibrated: nominal 90% intervals covered approximately 62% of reference values, with boundary spread artifacts and reduced skill under sparser observations.
paper_title: BridgeSRDA: Efficient Probabilistic Super-Resolution Data Assimilation with Forecast-Informed Stochastic Interpolants
